chapter: Club Alabam and the Europe contract
title: Succeeding Fletcher Henderson at the Club Alabam
summary: After a year at the Nest he takes over the Club Alabam, the first Times Square club, whose audience included Whiteman and Jack Dempsey.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, you hit on this sound and you're at the Nest. For how long are you at the Nest?
Oh, I was at the Nest, well a good year.
And then what happened to get you out of the Nest.
Well, nothing. This job. When Fletcher walked out, his mistake was my success.

Why, he walked out and we walked into the Club Alabam. That was on 44th Street under the Nora Bayes Theater, at the time. It was down in the basement. But it was -- and the thing of it was, now we had to add that third saxophone and put in a trombone. Otherwise the band was the same, see.
And what was the Club Alabam like?

The Club Alabam was like, there was in those days, the first club in New York, and the first club anywhere, was the Plantation Club. And Florence Mills played there with Sam Selvin. And after that was our club, the Club Alabam. And from then on, clubs all over the United States took that name, Club Alabam. You see, Club Alabam had such audience always as George Olson, Paul Whiteman, Vincent Lopez, Gloria Swanson, Firpo, Jack Dempsey and all, you know what I mean? It was the biggest thing in New York at the time.
It was right in the Times Square area.
But, any blacks come in there?

Now and then, if they were celebrities. But they didn't keep them out, but it was a little steep for their money at that time, and Harlem was so well, well we didn't ever leave Harlem. Harlem was something in those days.
And you could get anything you wanted in

Harlem and that was a job. And as soon after we finished rehearsing, right to Harlem we'd go. Nobody stayed around downtown. And I think we weren't thinking so much about integration then. You was just enjoying yourself, and to each his own.
